Playbook.name: AD — Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink Modified) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute was modified (5136/5137) on an account - the Shadow Credentials technique adds an attacker-controlled key so they can obtain that account's TGT/NTLM via PKINIT. Triage question: was this a legitimate device/WHfB enrolment or an attacker planting a key on a target account?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Shadow Credentials give persistent impersonation of the target (often a privileged user or computer) without touching its password.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Windows Hello for Business / Intune enrolment legitimately writes this attribute for the enrolling USER on their OWN object - one principal editing ANOTHER privileged account's key is the attack shape.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the key modification is self-enrolment (WHfB/device) or a third party planting credentials on another account.

Step.name: Who changed whose key, and is it self or cross-account
Step.Purpose: Self-write (subject == target) during enrolment is benign; cross-account write to a privileged target is the attack.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("5136","5137") AND winlog.event_data.AttributeLDAPDisplayName == "msDS-KeyCredentialLink" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL op = winlog.event_data.OperationType | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.ObjectDN, op | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: Compare SubjectUserName to the ObjectDN account. Enrolment: a user/device writing its own key, or ADFS/Intune connector accounts. Attack: an admin/service principal writing the key of a DIFFERENT, higher-value account.

Step.name: Modifier's recent privileged actions
Step.Purpose: If the modifier also touched DACLs, group memberships, or other key attributes, this is an active persistence campaign, not enrolment.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("5136","4728","4732","4756","4738","4670") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), targets = VALUES(winlog.event_data.ObjectDN) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: A modifier making several directory changes across objects in minutes is operating as an attacker/admin script; a lone self-enrolment writes only its own key once.

Step.name: Did the target account then authenticate via PKINIT/new source
Step.Purpose: Use of the planted key shows up as the target getting a TGT (4768) from a new source shortly after.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4768","4624") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS c = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY src | SORT first_seen ASC | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A TGT for the target from a new source right after the key change suggests the shadow credential is already being used.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows $username writing the KeyCredentialLink of a DIFFERENT account (especially privileged), not self-enrolment.
INV-02 shows the modifier making multiple directory changes across objects (active abuse).
INV-01 shows self-enrolment (subject writes its own key) or the known Intune/ADFS device-registration connector on the user's own object.
Cross-account write but modifier is a delegated IAM admin and no follow-on use - ownership unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SHADOW-WHO, INV-02-SHADOW-ACTOR, INV-03-SHADOW-USE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate Windows Hello for Business / device registration writing the key on the enrolling account's own object.

Indicators.Item: SubjectUserName equals the target account, or is the documented Intune/ADFS registration service.
One key write, no cross-account pattern.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the enrolment via Intune/WHfB logs.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker planted a key credential to impersonate the target account.

Indicators.Item: Cross-account key write, especially onto privileged or computer accounts.
Target obtains a TGT from a new source afterward.

SOCAction.Item: Remove the malicious msDS-KeyCredentialLink value from the target.
Reset the target and disable the modifier; contain the modifier's host.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An identity product mis-provisioned to write keys on objects it should not.

Indicators.Item: A sync/registration service writing keys on unexpected objects due to broad delegation.
Vendor confirms the intent is benign but over-scoped.

SOCAction.Item: Tighten the service's write scope on msDS-KeyCredentialLink.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Remove the attacker key value from $target_user.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reset the target account; revoke tickets; hunt for other planted keys across privileged objects.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Restrict who can write msDS-KeyCredentialLink; monitor this attribute continuously.

QualityChecks.Check: OperationType distinguishes add(1)/delete; verify field presence per DC.
WHfB rollout windows will elevate benign volume - coordinate with IAM.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Malicious key removed, target reset, modifier eradicated, other objects swept.
